structure: Single English PDF (2023 DC K-12 Social Studies Standards). Front matter (cover, TOC, OSSE message, role and organization of the standards), then 'Statements of Practice for Social Studies' (pp. 6-10: Inquiry Arc, History, Civics/Government/Human Rights, Geography, Economics competencies; K-12 skills, two-column page layout extracted in scrambled order). Content is organized as a grade/course overview page (table cell with title, theme and narrative, plus page-number cell), then pages of Driving Concepts. Each Driving Concept = heading 'Driving Concept N: title', a narrative description ('In this driving concept, students will...'), and numbered standards. Codes: K.1-K.27 (kindergarten), 1.1-1.35, 2.1-2.32, 3.1-3.42, 4.1-4.54, 5.1-5.56, 6.1-6.68, 7.1-7.80, 8.1-8.67 (grade level, numbering continuous across driving concepts); high school courses use prefixes WH1.n (World History I), WH2.n (World History II), US2.n (US History II: Reconstruction through the Present; 'US.56' is a typo for US2.56), GC.n (Government and Civics), DC.n (District of Columbia History and Government). Grade bands K-2, 3-5, 6-8, 9-12 appear as heading cells above the grade overview. Running headers inside the units (x~754) repeat the grade/course title and are labeled standards (title). Narrative driving-concept descriptions and grade/course overview narratives are labeled examples; no separate example/teacher-note blocks exist. Some units mix the last standard of one driving concept with the next driving concept heading or the 'STANDARD:' marker; those are labeled standards. High school courses are not tied to a single grade (9-12) and use the course title as written. Acknowledgements and back cover are backup.

u119,u287,u537,u846: grade-band heading cells (K-2, 3-5, 6-8, 9-12 STANDARDS) labeled standards with the band range; could alternatively be treated as backup.

u1139: narrative driving-concept description for US History II DC3 is merged in one unit with 'STANDARD:' and standards US2.27-US2.36; labeled standards. Similarly u1035 and u1057 (narrative + trailing 'STANDARD:' marker) labeled examples; u1142 (US2.37-2.42), u671 (7.15-7.28), u1139 contain multiple standards in one unit.
